title: Chet Hebrew Letter (ח): Sound & Furtive Patah
description: Learn the Hebrew letter Chet (ח): its guttural [ch] sound, the furtive Patah in כּוֹחַ (strength), words like אָח (brother), plus interactive practice.

editorialIssues.detail: Several letter-recognition distractors use letters (Nun, Lamed, Samekh, Ayin, Tav) not introduced in this lesson. Beginner scaffolding can be improved separately from the approved source synchronization.

blocks.0: Chet Hebrew Letter (ח): Sound, Furtive Patah & Practice
blocks.5: The word אָח [ach] means 'brother' and has one syllable. Kamatz Gadol under Aleph (אָ) represents [a]. Chet at the end of the word (ח) supplies [ch]. There is no vowel sign under Chet in this word.

theory.heading: Meet Chet
theory.intro: The eighth letter of the Hebrew alphabet. Chet makes a guttural [ch] sound, as in German “Bach” or Scottish “loch” — air flows continuously through a narrow space at the back of the mouth.
objectives: Hear its guttural [ch] sound, as in “Bach.”
Read Chet in real words like <bdi class="hebrew" lang="he" dir="rtl">אָח</bdi> (brother).

examples.heading: Chet in real words
examples.intro: See Chet in two new Hebrew words, and review the Segol, Holam Male and Shuruk vowel marks from earlier letters.
